root_cause.text: In `arch/s390/include/asm/fpu-insn.h`, the `fpu_vstl()` inline assembly store is variably sized at runtime based on `index`, but KMSAN/clang only instruments it as a 1-byte store from the compile-time constraints, leaving the actually written bytes marked uninitialized and triggering false-positive reports.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `#include <linux/kmsan.h>` and calls `kmsan_unpoison_memory(vxr, size);` immediately after the `vstl` asm in both `fpu_vstl()` variants, and the commit message explains that `vstl` “can write varied amount of bytes depending on value of 'index' argument” while “clang currently generates call to __msan_instrument_asm_store with 1 byte as size.”

intent_record.how: This makes KMSAN-related declarations/macros available to code including this header, enabling memory-sanitizer instrumentation support where needed at compile time.

intent_record.intent_summary: Mark memory written by `fpu_vstl()` as initialized so KMSAN does not report false uninitialized-memory warnings.
intent_record.what: A call to `kmsan_unpoison_memory(vxr, size);` was added immediately after the inline assembly in `fpu_vstl()`.
intent_record.how: After the FPU store operation writes to the destination buffer, the memory region is marked unpoisoned for KMSAN, preventing the sanitizer from treating the freshly written bytes as uninitialized on later reads.

intent_record.intent_summary: Mark the destination buffer as initialized after the FPU store to avoid KMSAN false positives.
intent_record.what: A call to `kmsan_unpoison_memory(vxr, size);` was added immediately after the inline assembly in `fpu_vstl()`.
intent_record.how: After the FPU store operation writes into the memory pointed to by `vxr`, that region is marked as initialized for KMSAN, preventing later false-positive uninitialized-memory reports when the stored bytes are read.

candidates.rationale: This inline-asm output constraint models the FPU store as a one-byte write to KMSAN/clang, even though the instruction can store a variably sized region based on index. That mismatch leaves the real destination bytes marked uninitialized.

This is the pre-fix asm output operand that constrains the compiler to a single-byte store. Because the actual fpu_vstl() write is larger depending on index, KMSAN instrumentation misses the full initialized range and reports false positives.

vuln_statements.explanation: This output constraint tells the compiler/KMSAN that the inline asm writes only one byte, while `fpu_vstl()` actually stores a runtime-sized region based on `index`. That mismatch is the root cause of the false uninitialized-memory reporting.

This is the same problematic single-byte output operand in the other variant of the inline asm. It under-describes the true variable-sized store, causing the bytes actually written by `fpu_vstl()` to remain marked uninitialized.

bic_trace_step.reason:
The snippet shows the exact vulnerable construct and its fix. The root cause is the `fpu_vstl()` inline assembly store being variably sized at runtime, but instrumented as only a 1-byte store by clang/KMSAN. In this diff, the previously clang-specific version was:

`asm volatile("VSTL\t%[v1],%[index],%O[vxr],%R[vxr]\n" : [vxr] "=Q" (*(u8 *)vxr) : [index] "d" (index), [v1] "I" (v1) : "memory");`

which is the vulnerable pattern because the output operand is only `*(u8 *)vxr` even though `size = min(index + 1, sizeof(__vector128));` shows the store length depends on `index`. The commit adds the corrected AOR-format branch using the same `VSTL` instruction but with the proper addressing form: `asm volatile("VSTL\t%[v1],%[index],%O[vxr],%R[vxr]\n" : [vxr] "=Q" (*(u8 *)vxr) : [index] "d" (index), [v1] "I" (v1) : "memory");` and moves the old non-AOR fallback to the `#else` path. This indicates the fix is present in the shown code. Because the function body itself clearly contains both the vulnerable pre-fix form and the fixed form chosen by `CONFIG_CC_HAS_ASM_AOR_FORMAT_FLAGS`, the snippet is sufficient to determine that the vulnerable construct exists in the pre-fix branch but the commit version already contains the fix for supported compilers.
